# Page indexing report

*Report* · also written Page indexing

The Search Console report that lists which URLs are indexed and why the others are not.

Narrative: the topic [Indexing statuses in Search Console](../topics/page-indexing-report.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

7 claims mention it: 2 from Google's documentation, 5 shown or said at the event (3 confirmed by Google docs, 2 consistent with Google docs). A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Page indexing report](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7440203?hl=en).

- [`D2-C707`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Docs: Google's Page indexing report help says a 'Discovered – currently not indexed' page was found but not crawled yet, typically because Google wanted to crawl it but expected the crawl to overload the site, so it rescheduled the crawl. `[D2-C707, docs, Google Search Console Help, https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7440203?hl=en]`
- [`D2-C712`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Docs: Google's Page indexing report help says a 'Crawled – currently not indexed' page was crawled but not indexed, may or may not be indexed in the future, and does not need to be resubmitted for crawling. `[D2-C712, docs, Google Search Console Help, https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7440203?hl=en]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D1-C368`](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) Stage, Day 1, confirmed by Google docs: Search Console's page indexing report breaks down the reasons why pages do or do not show in Search, and its categories help find patterns in how a site's content is crawled and served to Google's crawlers. `[D1-C368, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C508`](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) Stage, Day 1, confirmed by Google docs: Google said soft 404s, like some other problem categories, are looked up in Search Console's page indexing report, while other crawl issues are debugged in the Crawl Stats report. `[D1-C508, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 1]`
- [`D2-C718`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: Not-indexed reasons in the Page indexing report include pages excluded by a noindex rule and 'Alternate page with proper canonical tag'. `[D2-C718, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C697`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Index selection drops a document carrying a noindex rule if it was not already dropped earlier in processing (noindex is a likely but not certain reading of the transcript, supported by the later mention of noindex among the Page indexing report reasons). `[D2-C697, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C717`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Search Console's Page indexing report is the place to check for index selection issues, and its not-indexed reasons are useful when testing changes on a site. `[D2-C717, stage, Google, Day 2]`

## For developers

- `DEV-MON-01` **MUST** · Documented: Verify every production host in Search Console before launch (its own text names it)
- `DEV-MON-03` **SHOULD** · Documented: Watch the Page indexing report and treat its not-indexed reasons as a work list (5 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
